summary: Unexpected persistent 429s after reducing per-key rate window for bulk ingestion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer TagStream reported an increase in persistent 429 responses across multiple API keys after they applied a configuration change to reduce their per-key rate window from 60s to 10s for faster short-burst throughput. The errors started immediately after the change and did not subside despite reducing client concurrency.

Impact:
- Multiple ingest jobs failing with 429s for ~40% of requests over a 3 hour window.
- Affects three production pipelines that write embeddings and chat convo history; customer reports downstream failures and job retries.
- Tenant is on a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity; billing unaffected but availability degraded.

Environment:
- prod: us-east (dedicated pool id dp-88)
- Keys impacted: 3 active API keys reported by customer (two short-lived worker keys and one long-lived service key)

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1. Toggle per-key window from 60s to 10s via Console policy UI for tenant tagstream-prod.
2. Start concurrent uploader (50 workers, 5 threads each) using short-lived keys minted for parallel workers.
3. Observe ~10-40% 429s starting within 2 minutes, persisting even after ramp down to 10 workers.

Observed logs/snippets (customer):
- "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests - token_bucket_exceeded per_key_window=10s tenant_quota=burst"
- Traces attached by customer: trace ids t-20260310-1002xx (uploader)

Customer expectation:
They expected the shorter window to allow more frequent micro-bursts per key (same aggregate throughput), not to trigger sustained throttling. They request guidance and a mitigation to restore steady-state throughput while keeping short window semantics.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: reducing per-key window moved accounting into the tenant-level burst controller, causing more frequent token accounting and early tenant bucket exhaustion when many short-lived keys were minted.
What we checked so far:
- Rate-limiter logs (rl-logs-prod-us-east) show spike in per_key token consumption events immediately after config change at 2026-03-10T09:57:21Z.
- Tenant token bucket drained faster due to token-count rounding when window < 30s; per-key granular accounting created higher effective cost when keys are short-lived.
- Scheduler logs show increased queueing for dedicated pool dp-88 at the same window, with fallback to 429 instead of queue spillover due to conservative queue config.
- No GPU capacity or serving-runtime OOM observed; CPU and memory within normal thresholds.
- Related config: console policy applied "per_key_window_seconds=10" and "allow_key_fanout=true".

Preliminary conclusion: the policy change altered the interaction between per-key windows and tenant burst accounting, making token leakage and rounding more visible when many ephemeral keys are minted.
timeline:
2026-03-10 09:55 - Customer opens ticket and applies config change via Console.
2026-03-10 09:57 - Support receives alert from customer about 429 spike.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support triage: assign to rate-limiter on-call.
2026-03-10 10:18 - Rate-limiter engineer (Miguel) starts log correlation and identifies per_key accounting spike.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Temporary mitigation recommended to customer: revert window to 60s and reduce short-lived key fanout.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Customer reverts to 60s and reports immediate reduction in 429s; some lanes still show residual 429s for 15 minutes.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Follow-up: create internal task to improve accounting when window < 30s.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:08 - Miguel Torres (Support): Logged initial findings. Noted that tenant dp-88 shows token drift. Asking SRE to check queue spillover thresholds: #support channel linked: https://slack.redwood.com/support.

2026-03-10 10:27 - Lena Brooks (SRE): Confirmed queues did not spill to fallback; cluster autoscaler not triggered due to reserved pool sizing. Seeing rate-limiter event bursts matching customer actions. Added label 'rate-limit-investigation'.

2026-03-10 11:05 - TagStream (Customer contact: marc.garcia@tagstream.com): Reverted window to 60s and observed drop in 429s. Customer requests written guidance so they can re-test with short windows safely.

2026-03-11 09:22 - Miguel Torres (Support): Follow-up with engineering proposal: adjust tenant token rounding and add a minimum accounting window in the rate-limiter for windows <30s. Opening internal PR to instrument metrics.
resolution_notes: Customer reverted per-key window to 60s which restored normal behavior. Support documented the interaction and delivered a short-term recommendation doc. Engineering will introduce a safety floor in the rate-limiter to avoid token rounding penalties for windows below 30s. No code change was rolled to production during incident window.
follow_up_actions:
1) Engineering task INT-451: Implement minimum accounting window (30s) and improve metrics for ephemeral key fanout.
2) Docs: update Console guidance on per-key window and ephemeral key best practices (owner: DX docs).
3) Support: send customer playbook with recommended settings for short-lived keys and example retry/backoff strategies.
4) Post-incident: add a canary test that simulates ephemeral key burst to dedicated pools during policy changes.
